earlier_scan.note: Only known material is Thomas 1910, a 12-page wordlist; no phonological description located

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiọmamhẹ. 1989. Comparative Edoid: Phonology and Lexicon. (Delta Series 6.) Port Harcourt: University of Port Harcourt Press.
sources.note: Comparative-historical phonology and lexicon; Glottolog lists Okpe [okx] among the languages with data; the introductory chapters describe the phonology (including tone) of the sampled Edoid languages and Proto-Edoid; the most likely place for any published remark on Okpe prosody.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiọmamhẹ. 1989. Edoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 291-304. Lanham: University Press of America.
sources.note: Family-level sketch with a phonology section (tone systems of Edoid); would supply at most a family-level tone statement, not an Okpe-specific one.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, John Muniru, David Onoja, Lewinan Andrew and Samuel Eju. 2024. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Five Southern Northwestern Edoid Languages in Southern Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2024-012. Dallas: SIL International. 72 pp. ISSN 2766-9327. (Glottolog ref 700271)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Sec. 8.3 gives tentative consonant inventory (Table 7) and a seven-vowel system /i e ɛ a ɔ o u/ (Table 9) for Okpe, Orake, Akhukhu, Okpamheri; notes on [ŋʷ], labialized and palatalized consonants, sporadic long vowels, no nasal vowels in Okpe, CV syllable preference; 222-item wordlist in Appendix F where the Okpe column carries no tone marks (Orake and Oloma columns have some). Tone explicitly not analysed; the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur. So: wordlist plus segmental sketch, no prosodic statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation; and Blench's Edoid wordlist/documents page.
sources.note: Entry for Okpe (Akoko-Edo) would list dialects (Idesa, Akuku) and any unpublished wordlists or manuscripts; Blench's site is captcha-could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Lewis, 'Demola. 2016. A Leipzig-Jakarta Vocabulary Reconstruction and Sound Correspondence based Sub-grouping of North Edoid. Extended abstract with appendices (Leipzig-Jakarta 100-word lists for North-Western and North-Central Edoid), 16 pp. Towards Proto-Niger-Congo: Comparison and Reconstruction, 2nd International Congress, Paris, 1-3 September 2016 (LLACAN).
sources.note: No prose on tone or stress (the words tone/stress/accent do not occur). But the appendix gives c. 90 Okpe (okx) Leipzig-Jakarta items in phonetic transcription WITH tone diacritics -- acute, grave and macron, e.g. 'arm/hand' éhà, 'ash' íḿ, 'back' ókókó, 'bird' āférì, 'black' órìrì, 'bone' úxwà, 'to come' ēlé, 'dog' àròkòmí, 'to drink' kíẃwù, 'to eat' īrésì, 'tongue' úr̀mì, 'tooth' ák̄, 'wind' òhéhé -- i.e. the first open tone-marked Okpe (NWE) data located; three diacritics are used (acute, grave and a macron level), no downstep sign in the Okpe column. This is data, not a statement of the to…

sources.citation: Lewis, Demola [Ademola Anthony]. 2015. Deciphering Aborigines and Migrants from Cognation and Topography in North-Western Edo. Lengua y migracion / Language and Migration 7(1): 29-51. Universidad de Alcala. hdl:10017/22658
sources.note: no phonology content: lexicostatistic cognation percentages (100/200/400-word scales), migration and topography; no transcribed Okpe forms with tone, no statement on tone or stress.

sources.note: no phonology content; the entry has no field 7-9 (sources/phonology) and no 'Refs.' line at all, i.e. Blench knows no published or unpublished linguistic source for the cluster (contrast neighbouring entry Ọkpamheri which cites a phonology).

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Francis O. 2011. The sound of meaning. Inaugural lecture, University of Ibadan.
sources.note: Nothing on Okpe phonology; only sociolinguistic notes (Okpe, Ososo, Somorika are 'mixed communities'; 'Idesa dialect of Okpe (a NWE language)'; Okpe is a one-village NWE community in Akoko-Edo; Ibadan-400 wordlists were collected for all North Edo communities).

sources.citation: Pogoson, Ohioma I. and Francis O. Egbokhare (eds.). 2002. New Perspectives in Edoid Studies: Essays in Honour of Ronald Peter Schaefer. (CASAS Book Series 20.) Cape Town: Centre for Advanced Studies of African Society. ISBN 1-919799-68-0. 154 pp. scan in the University of Ibadan repository.
sources.note: no content on Okpe (NWE); volume concerns Edo (Bini), Emai and Ora.

sources.citation: Pulleyblank, Douglas. 1986. Underspecification and low vowel harmony in Okpe. Studies in African Linguistics 17(2).
sources.note: Not this language: the Okpe of the vowel-harmony literature is the Southwestern Edoid Okpe of Delta State (Hoffmann 1973 data; 'closely related language Uvwie'), i.e. okpe1250/oke. downloaded only to settle the identity of the Hérault/Prescott entries in Glottolog's list; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiọmamhẹ. 1973. A comparative Edo phonology. PhD thesis, University of Ibadan.
sources.note: Precursor of Comparative Edoid; may include Okpe/Akoko-Edo data with tone; whether it covers okx is unverified.

sources.citation: Thomas, Northcote W. 1910. Anthropological Report on the Edo-Speaking Peoples of Nigeria, Part II: Linguistics (incl. 'Texts in other languages of the Edo family', pp. 71-128, and 'Comparative dictionary of selected words in the Edo languages', pp. 151-186). London: Harrison and Sons.
sources.note: Nothing for Okpe. The Okpe material is three untoned, unstressed texts (pp. 106-108, 'Okpe. Southern Nigeria. (3 texts.)', interpreted via Yoruba by Corporal Nimahan) plus 'Ok.' columns in the comparative dictionary. The only 'Accent and tone' section (pp. 141-142: 'The dynamic accent falls normally on the penultimate..') sits inside the EDO (Bini) grammar and does not refer to Okpe; the preface admits tones 'have been omitted in many cases'.

sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Confirm identity (okx = Okpe of Akoko-Edo, subgroup Okpe-Akuku-Idesa okpe1251) and that Glottolog counts zero descriptive references for the language.
